extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (persons preparing Office actions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory practices for USPTO patent examiners in drafting Office actions, responding to amendments and arguments, handling claims, and managing prosecution order and mailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note All Outstanding Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In taking up an amended application for action the examiner should note in every letter all the requirements outstanding against the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every point in the prior action of an examiner which is still applicable must be repeated or referred to, to prevent the implied waiver of the requirement. Such requirements include requirements for information under 37 CFR 1.105 and MPEP § 704.10; however the examiner should determine whether any such requirement has been satisfied by a negative reply under 37 CFR 1.105(a)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Require Correction of Informalities When Allowable Subject Matter Found
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as allowable subject matter is found, correction of all informalities then present should be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should require correction of informalities immediately upon finding allowable subject matter to expedite allowance and prevent avoidable delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer All Material Traversed / Provide Clear Explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner must provide clear explanations of all actions taken by the examiner during prosecution of an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where requirements are traversed or suspension requested, make proper reference thereto in action on the amendment. If applicant traverses any rejection and the examiner repeats the rejection, the examiner should take note of the applicant’s argument and answer the substance of it. Provide a complete application file history and enhance clarity of the prosecution record.

rubrics_metrics.name: When Withdrawing a Previous Rejection, State Specific Reasons and Citations
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant’s arguments are persuasive and the examiner determines the previous rejection should be withdrawn, the examiner must provide in the next Office communication the reasons why the previous rejection is withdrawn by referring specifically to the page(s) and line(s) of applicant’s remarks which form the basis for withdrawing the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not acceptable to merely indicate that all of applicant’s remarks form the basis. Form paragraph 7.38.01 may be used. If withdrawal results in allowance, the reasons may be included in a reasons for allowance (see MPEP § 1302.14).

rubrics_metrics.name: If Withdrawing But Adding New Ground, Use Proper Form Paragraph and Check Finality
rubrics_metrics.description: If the previous rejection is withdrawn but a new ground of rejection should be made upon further consideration, form paragraph 7.38.02 may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 706.07(a) to determine whether the Office action may be made final. In form paragraph 7.38.02, identify pages/lines of applicant's remarks and insert statutory basis and new ground(s) with explanation (e.g., different interpretation, newly found prior art).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify Rejection of Record Applied to New/Amended Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If a rejection of record is to be applied to a new or amended claim, specific identification of that ground of rejection should be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite the paragraph in the former Office letter in which the rejection was originally stated so applicant can trace the basis for the rejection being reapplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider and Respond to Asserted Advantages
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicant argues that prior art does not teach or inherently yield one or more advantages (new or improved results), the examiner should state reasons if those advantages are insufficient to overcome the rejection(s) of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State reasons in the record, preferably in the action following the assertion so applicant and, if appealed, the Board will know the advantages were considered. See MPEP § 716 et seq. for affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.132. The failure to rebut persuasive advantage statements may lead to allowance (see In re Herrmann, In re Soni).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Form Paragraph 7.37 for Unpersuasive Arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant’s arguments are not persuasive, form paragraphs 7.37 through 7.37.13 may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ¶7.37 requires the examiner to state that applicant’s arguments have been fully considered but are not persuasive and to provide explanation as to non-persuasiveness. Form paragraphs for particular unpersuasive argument types must be preceded by ¶7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address All Arguments Not Previously Responded To
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must address all arguments which have not already been responded to in the statement of the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When repeating a rejection, the examiner should take note of applicant’s arguments and answer the substance to avoid leaving material unaddressed in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Age of References
rubrics_metrics.description: Contentions that the reference patents are old are not impressive absent a showing that the art tried and failed to solve the same problem notwithstanding presumed knowledge of the references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶7.37.01; precede with ¶7.37. Cite In re Wright as authority. Briefly restate applicant’s argument about age where indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Bodily Incorporation
rubrics_metrics.description: The test for obviousness is not whether features of a secondary reference may be bodily incorporated into the primary reference; rather, the test is what the combined teachings would have suggested to one of ordinary skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶7.37.02 (preceded by ¶7.37). Briefly restate applicant’s bodily incorporation argument in bracketed text. Cite In re Keller.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Hindsight Reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Although obviousness judgments involve reconstruction, they are proper if they take into account only knowledge within the level of ordinary skill at the time and do not include knowledge gleaned only from the applicant’s disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶7.37.03 (preceded by ¶7.37). Cite In re McLaughlin. Explain why the rejection is not based on improper hindsight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: No Suggestion to Combine
rubrics_metrics.description: Obviousness can be established by combining or modifying teachings of prior art where there is teaching, suggestion, or motivation to do so found in the references or in knowledge generally available to one of ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶7.37.04 (preceded by ¶7.37). Explain where motivation for the rejection is found (in references or general knowledge). Cite In re Fine and In re Jones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Nonanalogous Art
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior art reference must either be in the field of the applicant’s endeavor or be reasonably pertinent to the particular problem concerned to be relied upon for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶7.37.05 (preceded by ¶7.37). Identify the reference and explain why it is analogous or pertinent. Cite In re Oetiker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Number of References
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliance on a large number of references in a rejection does not, without more, weigh against obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶7.37.06 (preceded by ¶7.37). Cite In re Gorman.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Applicant Obtains Result Not Contemplated by Prior Art
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition of another advantage flowing naturally from following the suggestion of the prior art cannot form the basis for patentability when differences would otherwise be obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶7.37.07 (preceded by ¶7.37). Cite Ex parte Obiaya.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Arguing Limitations Not Claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: Features relied upon by applicant that are not recited in the rejected claim(s) are not given patentable weight; limitations from the specification are not read into the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶7.37.08 (preceded by ¶7.37). Recite the features applicant relies upon and explain they are not claimed. Cite In re Van Geuns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Intended Use
rubrics_metrics.description: A recitation of intended use must result in a structural difference between the claimed invention and the prior art to distinguish patentably; for process claims, intended use must result in a manipulative difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶7.37.09 (preceded by ¶7.37). Explain why intended use does or does not impart patentable weight. Cite In re Casey and In re Otto.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Preamble Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: A preamble is generally not accorded patentable weight where it merely recites purpose or intended use and the body of the claim stands alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶7.37.10 (preceded by ¶7.37). Restate the preamble recitation and explain lack of patentable weight. Cite In re Hirao and Kropa v. Robie.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: General Allegation of Patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s general allegation that the claims define a patentable invention fails to comply with 37 CFR 1.111(b) unless it specifically points out how the claim language patentably distinguishes over the references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶7.37.11 (preceded by ¶7.37). Require specificity per the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Novelty Not Clearly Pointed Out
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s arguments must clearly point out the patentable novelty presented in view of the state of the art disclosed by the references, per 37 CFR 1.111(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶7.37.12 (preceded by ¶7.37). Explain how amendments avoid references or objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Arguing Against References Individually
rubrics_metrics.description: One cannot show nonobviousness by attacking references individually where rejections are based on combinations of references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶7.37.13 (preceded by ¶7.37). Cite In re Keller and In re Merck & Co.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Piecemeal Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Piecemeal examination should be avoided as much as possible; the examiner ordinarily should reject each claim on all valid grounds available, avoiding undue multiplication of references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply major technical rejections (e.g., lack of disclosure, enablement, serious indefiniteness, res judicata) with full development of reasons rather than mere conclusions. Do not make secondary rejections on minor grounds where prior art discloses the 'heart' of the invention. Recognize language limitations and avoid premature negative limitations or indefiniteness rejections when an improved mode of definition is not known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations Where Limiting Examination to an Issue is Acceptable
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain situations justify limiting action on claims to a particular issue rather than full examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such situations include: (A) application too informal for complete action (MPEP § 702.01); (B) undue multiplicity of claims with no election (MPEP § 2173.05(n)); (C) misjoinder of inventions with no successful election (MPEP § 803, § 806.02, § 812.01); (D) disclosure directed to perpetual motion (use best prior art and point out pertinency but not necessarily apply it to claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: When Major Technical Rejection Proper, Fully Develop Reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a major technical rejection is proper it should be stated with a full development of reasons rather than by a mere conclusion coupled with some stereotyped expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major rejections include lack of proper disclosure, lack of enablement, serious indefiniteness and res judicata. Provide substantive reasoning in the Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each Claim Must Be Mentioned in Every Office Action
rubrics_metrics.description: In every office action, each pending claim should be mentioned by number, and its treatment or status given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since a claim keeps its numeral through prosecution, this practice aids traceability. Each action should conclude with a summary of all claims presented for examination. Claims retained under 37 CFR 1.142 and 1.146 should be treated per MPEP § 821–821.03 and § 809.02(c). Keep Index of Claims up to date per MPEP § 719.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting Claims for Pro Se Applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner believes an applicant is unfamiliar with proper preparation, the examiner may draft one or more claims and indicate such claims would be allowed if incorporated by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice expedites prosecution and offers service to unrepresented inventors; it is desirable and permissible where appropriate. If the suggested claim is not embraced by the original oath/declaration, require supplemental oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.67. Use form paragraph 7.43.04 and indicate complete text of suggested claim(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable Except As To Form — Offer Definite Suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: When application discloses patentable subject matter but claims cannot be allowed because of defects in form or omission, the examiner should not stop with a bare objection; offer a definite suggestion for correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner’s action should be constructive and may suggest an interview to accelerate agreement on allowable claims. If certain aspects are not claimed, note that and indicate that if properly claimed such claims may be favorably considered. If a claim is allowable but dependent on canceled/rejected claim, state it would be allowable if rewritten in independent form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate Allowable Subject Matter / Early Allowance of Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When the prior art has been fully developed and some claims are clearly allowable, the allowance of such claims should not be delayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 7.43, 7.43.01, 7.43.02 may be used to indicate allowable subject matter. Use ¶7.97 to indicate claim allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment on Examples and Test Results Carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Results of tests and examples should not normally be questioned unless there is a reasonable basis; if questioned, appropriate claims should be rejected as being based on insufficient disclosure under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must reply with actual test results or relevant arguments showing strong reason to believe the predicted result; avoid introduction of new matter. If operability or utility is in doubt, consider rejection under 35 U.S.C. 101 (see MPEP § 706.03(a) and § 2107 et seq.). See MPEP §§ 2161–2164.08(c) for written description and enablement guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing and Initialing by Assistant Examiner — Provide Contact Info
rubrics_metrics.description: The full surname of the examiner who prepares the Office action must be typed at the end of the action; the telephone number below should be called if application is to be discussed or interview arranged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.100, 7.101 or 7.102 at conclusion of all actions to provide contact name/phone. After the action is typed, the preparing examiner reviews it for correctness; the surname or initials and date typed should appear; if not authorized to sign, initial above typed name and forward to authorized signatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number Paragraphs of Office Actions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is good practice to number the paragraphs of the Office action consecutively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbering facilitates identification of paragraphs in future prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide Telephone Inquiry Contacts with Required Details
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Office action should include the name and telephone number of the examiner to be contacted, duty hours, and supervisor/receptionist/fax numbers where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶7.101 or ¶7.102 templates. Insert examiner name, individual phone, normal duty hours/days, supervisor name and phone, organization fax, and receptionist phone as indicated in the form paragraph instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing by Authorized Examiner Promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: All Office actions and other correspondence should be signed promptly by the authorized examiner; only the original is signed but the word 'Examiner' and signer name should appear on original and copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the original signed copy is placed properly in the file wrapper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry and Mailing Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The original signed action is placed in the file wrapper; its character, paper number and date of mailing are entered in black ink on the outside of the file wrapper under 'Contents.' Mailing date should be stamped or printed after signing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of action are mailed by the Technology Center after original has been placed in the file and initialed/signed. After mailing, original is returned for placement in the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for Returned Office Actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Office action is returned undelivered by USPS, the examiner should attempt to ascertain the correct address and forward the action again, stamping 'remailed' and redirecting if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If action was addressed to an attorney, consider informing inventor or assignee. The period runs from remailing (the period dating from remailing). If repeated delivery fails, place letter and envelope in file wrapper; if the period dating from remailing elapses with no communication, the application is abandoned. See Ex parte Gourtoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of Examination and Priority Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonprovisional applications accepted as complete are assigned to Technology Centers and taken up for examination in the order filed except for those advanced under 37 CFR 1.102; examiners give priority in their docket to the application with the oldest effective U.S. filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain cases (reissues, reexaminations, litigation-related, special cases with fixed due dates) receive priority. Amended applications are taken up in order determined by the Commissioner. Respond to all amendments before final rejection within two months of receipt. The actual filing date of a CIP is used for docketing but examiner may use effective filing date if desired. Correct any errors in effective filing date status promptly via technical support staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for Making an Application Special / Petition To Make Special
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications will not be advanced out of turn except as provided or upon Commissioner order, or upon filing of a request or petition under 37 CFR 1.102; petitions to make special may be granted for certain statutory reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: advancement for inventions of peculiar importance upon government request; petitions without fee for applicant’s age or health or inventions enhancing environment or energy; other petitions must be accompanied by fee per §1.17(h). List of special cases (A–J) enumerates situations warranting advancement (e.g., reissue in stayed litigation, remand by appellate tribunal, interference, cases ready for allowance, cases pending >5 years, etc.). Once an application is made special, it generally remains special throughout prosecution subject to diligent prosecution by applicant.
